transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

That 'crashing' sound is probably a mechanical issue with the door balance system rather than an electrical fault. In built-in dishwashers, heavy doors are held open by springs or cables running through the hinges; when these stretch, snap, or come off their mounts, gravity takes over and the door drops. To confirm this, please look at the hinge area on both sides of the door with it fully open: can you see two springs (or cables) connecting the hinge arms to the cabinet frame? Are they still attached at both ends and do they look taut or slack?
I looked under the plinth at the sides with a torch and on the right side I can see a spring just hanging loose. The left one still seems to have some tension. I heard a twang last week when it went.

The 'twang' you heard last week suggests that the right-hand spring has snapped. Because one side is now slack and hanging loose while the other still has tension, the door can no longer stay open and will crash down when you pull it. This is a standard mechanical wear part; the spring needs to be replaced. As this involves removing the door assembly and handling tensioned components, I recommend contacting an engineer to fit the new spring safely.

candidates: Worn door balance springs or hinge cables (high)
